System Map

Read together, the four themes are not separate pressures. Five loops connect them. Dearer boats, fewer owners (R1): running costs stop people owning, and thinner club income pushes costs onto those who remain. Supplied boats bring new sailors (R2): boats the club supplies bring in young sailors, who make league teams that need fleets. Protection closes anchorages (B1): anchoring damages restored seabed, and protection closes the area. Chargers bring electric boats (R3), while fire risk slows batteries (B2). Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

Hover over a status for its meaning: Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now; Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether loop R2 (supplied boats bring new sailors) takes over from loop R1 (dearer boats, fewer owners), that is whether members sail their own boats or boats the club supplies; its vertical axis asks how far loop B1 (protection closes anchorages) and rising seas reach, that is whether the Solent stays open or becomes restricted.

What it means: the same rising cost that drives loop R1 can drive loop R2 instead, if the club supplies the boats: cost then pushes people towards the club rather than away from it. The levers the club controls are what it supplies, how it carries young sailors into racing, how well it knows its exposure on the water, and when it plans the marina's power.
